lines.why: Yellow-framed temporary construction fence panels on concrete feet along the Confederation Centre's Victoria Row side (the $65M library-wing rebuild). signs.why: What's left of the Sir John A. Macdonald statue (bronze man on a bench, removed by council at dawn on 1 June 2021, crated at the Public Works yard since, 'no plans' in 2024): a waist-high grey stone post with a sloped bronze plaque on top, and beside it the bare concrete pad the bench was bolted to, set in the brick paving, with traces of red paint. The real plaque is about Macdonald; we can't name him, so either leave it blank (text '') or use this line, which is aimed at council's indecision, not at anyone else. Ask Joe before using the text.

Approved Dec 2021 as a 4.3 x 4.6 m vinyl on a tension frame. A real artwork: make our own picture in the same spirit (three figures, flat colours, blue ground) rather than copy it. landmark_fixes.name: The Old Triangle (pub), Great George at Fitzroy
landmark_fixes.change: First pass guessed a brick commercial block; CBC's aerial and council photos show a two-and-a-half-storey wooden building painted barn red (#b5524a), vertical board / narrow clapboard siding, white trim, a steep gabled dark-grey roof with its long side on Fitzroy Street and the gable end facing south over a parking lot, ground-floor pub front at the Great George corner; behind it a wooden-fenced back patio with picnic tables and umbrellas. Address 189 Great George per CBC (OSM says 89). Suggested: style clapboard, colour #b5524a, roof gabled, roof_colour #3c3f43, trim white, shop true. Keep stand-in name 'The Old Rectangle' (no real business found).

landmark_fixes.name: Corner block at Queen and Victoria Row (south-east corner)
landmark_fixes.change: No entry yet. Four-storey red brick Victorian commercial block (#8e3f2e) with red sandstone string courses and a stone name band high on the Queen Street front reading '...1892 BLOCK' (partly read), tall arched upper windows, a canted/pilastered corner; ground floor shops under black-and-white striped awnings and a dark green fascia with gold script, #110. A souvenir shop with a green diamond-shaped hanging sign. The corner plaza in front of it is where the statue sat. Suggested: style brick, colour #8e3f2e, trim #b9785b (sandstone), cornice true, shop true, awning '#1c1c1c' striped if supported.

landmark_fixes.name: Victoria Row brick row (south side of Richmond, Queen to the Legislative parking lot)
landmark_fixes.change: No entries yet. One continuous Victorian commercial row of three/four-storey red brick (#8b4030 to #9a4a35), round-arched and segmental upper windows with stone heads in rhythm, corbelled brick cornices, some cast-iron shopfronts. Ground floors: cafés and restaurants with dark painted fronts (navy, black, deep green), black or navy fabric awnings with white script, hanging blade signs, string lights from the fronts to tall black posts at the patio edge. Use stand-in names only.

Known downtown murals: a huge geometric animal-faces mural (cats/owls in faceted pink, green, teal, orange) on 89 Kent Street (OSM gives that address to Fire Station No. 1; which wall is a guess); one on the rear of 151 Great George; one on 64 King Street (all 2022, Kent Street revitalisation); the Old Triangle gable (see signs); and a planned mural on the long low grey concrete retaining wall along the brick walk in front of the library (Dominion Building), finalists chosen July 2026, none from the Island (that wall is still blank in the game).

street_feel: Victoria Row is closed to cars from about May to October (and was fully fenced Jan 2025 to June 2026 for the Confederation Centre work). The game currently parks cars on it (generated parked_car props between Queen and Great George). In season it should have no parked cars and no through traffic, only patios, people, and the occasional delivery van at dawn.

Victoria Row in summer: brick-paved street the full width, red brick four-storey row on the south side, the Confederation Centre's ribbed sandstone wall on the north, iron arches with bulbs at both ends, black lantern lamps, street trees (Norway maples) in the sidewalk on the shop side, patios with black iron railings and flower boxes, umbrellas (black, lime green), string lights. Busker or two by the Queen end.

The corner at Queen and Victoria Row: the bronze statue on the bench was the most photographed thing downtown until 1 June 2021; now a bare concrete pad in the brick, a plaque post and half-barrel planters. Locals still call it 'where John A. was'. Don't put the statue back.

Queen Square around Province House: the restored grey-buff sandstone building with the three-soldier war memorial on its Grafton side (already placed), a round stone feature ringed by benches behind the memorial, red-tinted paths, flower beds and mulch, lamp posts with banners. On Remembrance Day the cenotaph gets wreath rails and the Grafton/Great George crosswalks are red and white.

Province House: closed since 2015 (estimated 3-5 years and $20M; now near $140M). Fences round the grounds were due to come down summer 2026 and the building to reopen fall 2026; MLAs still weren't back in spring 2026.

Rochford Square ('The Bog'): a quiet square of big old trees, an asphalt diagonal path, a round carpet bed of red/yellow/white annuals in the middle, clipped hedges, black lantern lamps, picnic tables, St. Peter's red-brick cathedral and All Souls' Chapel on the north-west side and the beige Shaw Building to the south-west. No playground. Emancipation Day (1 August) fills it with tents, a small stage and a string of flags; a permanent marker for The Bog (the 19th-century Black neighbourhood) is being planned (consultations Sept 2026), not yet built.

Sydney Street between Queen and Great George is the other patio street: patios built out into the parking lane with chunky wooden planter boxes and black iron railings, lights strung across the street, St. Dunstan's spires at the end of the view. The district master plan (2023, $10-14M, unfunded) would close parts of it to cars part of the year.
Kent Street from Great George to Prince: overhead lights strung lamp post to lamp post (approved 2022) and three big murals on side walls; a mix of 1970s brick offices and older wood.

City Hall (Queen and Kent): red brick with a corner clock tower, three flagpoles on the corner lawn, a two-faced post clock at the corner, a one-way sign. Banners on downtown lamp posts change with the season (veterans' banners in November).
Downtown bike parking is short; bikes get locked to meters, lamp posts and fences. Scattered rusty grid racks.
The T3 downtown stop is on Queen by the Confederation Centre (already in transit.json as 'Queen St / Confederation Centre'); no extra shelter proposed.
